title: Signal & Counterplay: LLM API Competitive Battlecard
content:
Purpose:
Quick operational guide for SDRs, AEs, and Solutions Engineers when positioning Redwood against general LLM API providers (hosted-only or single-mode vendors). Focus: signals to listen for, prioritized counters, demo hooks, pricing traps, and objection scripts that map to buyer concerns (cost, reliability, security, ops).

TL;DR (30s):
- Signal: Customer complains about unpredictable token costs, noisy latency spikes, or vendor lock-in.
- Counter: Redwood = predictable economics + multi-mode serving (hosted + dedicated + private) + routing fallbacks.
- Demo hook: Show per-route latency/cost heatmap + an autoscaling policy tied to a canary rollout.

Buyer personas & prioritized signals:
1) Platform/Infra (SRE, infra eng)
- Signals: “We can’t tolerate regional outages”, “need VPC/on-prem option”, “strict KMS/HSM policy”.
- Counterplay: Redwood Private + private control plane + KMS integrations + circuit-breaker routing between regions.
- Trap question to ask: "What SLOs have they missed in the last quarter?"

2) Product/ML Engineers
- Signals: "Latency spikes when traffic bursts", "we need consistent KV cache behavior for chat apps"
- Counterplay: Explain continuous batching, KV cache management, and kernel-selection logic that preserves latency tail while enabling batching. Share latency percentiles for comparable models.

3) Finance/Procurement
- Signals: "Vendor is cheaper per-token but invoices are volatile", "hard to forecast ops cost"
- Counterplay: Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching & quantization), reserved capacity for committed costs, token-level and request-level cost breakdowns for forecasting. Offer a short model-quantization savings scenario.

4) Security/Compliance
- Signals: "We need audit logs and SOC2/GDPR controls"
- Counterplay: Private deployment options, audit trail, enterprise support and compliance add-ons, air-gapped packaging.

Top competitive signals (what prospects often say) and our short counters:
- "They have a cheaper per-token rate." -> "Compare on total unit economics: queueing, retries, tail latency, and engineering time to build routing/fallbacks. We can run a 2-week cost/capacity pilot and show delta."
- "We already have a general cloud LLM endpoint." -> "Most general endpoints lack predictable SLOs, dedicated capacity, and private deployment options. We partner to migrate inference serving with minimal app changes and better observability."
- "We don’t want vendor lock-in." -> "Redwood’s API parity across hosted/dedicated/private means you can start hosted, then move to private with same interface and minimal refactor."

Technical rebuttals & evidence snippets (for SEs):
- Latency consistency: "Our serving runtime uses workload-aware kernel selection + continuous batching; in customer X pilot we kept p99 under 800ms at 10k rps with median < 150ms (internal report available)."
- Failover policies: "Smart routing can fallback to a smaller model variant or regional pool automatically; demo script: throttle primary pool and show automatic fallback without app errors."
- Cost optimization: "Optimize engine suggests batching configs and quantization per-model; show before/after cost per 1M tokens with and without Optimize applied."

Common buyer objections and scripts:
- Objection: "We can build these features in-house."
  - Script: "True, but building a production-grade serving runtime + autoscaler + KV cache + observability is 12–18 months for a small infra team and still often lacks cost transparency; Redwood packages this with SLOs, capacity contracts, and operations tooling so your team ships ML features instead of building infra."
- Objection: "Their SLAs are similar."
  - Script: "Ask what their SLA covers: single-region vs multi-region, token latency vs request latency, and whether they provide per-route dashboards and regression alerts. Redwood’s Dedicated contracts include latency targets and rollback policies driven by evals."
- Objection: "We’re worried about query data leaving our VPC."
  - Script: "Point to our Private deployment and enterprise packaging—control plane can be customer-managed; we also support KMS/HSM and offer audit logs for data access."

Demo play (5–8 minutes):
1) Start: Run a short chat prompt that includes a heavy context and show baseline latency and token usage.
2) Cost view: Switch to the per-route cost breakdown and show token-level segmentation (prompt vs completion).
3) Failure simulation: Inject a capacity fault and show smart routing fallback to a compatible model variant + automatic rollback.
4) Optimize: Toggle a suggested batching/quantization profile and show projected monthly savings.

Pricing traps to call out (coach AEs):
- Watch for "token-only" comparisons — push to compare system-level cost (retries, compute overhead, occasional re-runs).
- Competitor "flat-rate" pitch that caps tokens at hidden throttles — ask about throttles and overage behavior.
- Free-tier usage pattern risks: show how bursty traffic can escalate from free-tier to expensive overages; offer: 30-day pilot with usage guardrails and a migration cost model.

One-liners & soundbites (for pitch moments):
- "Predictable inference economics, not just cheaper tokens."
- "Same API whether hosted, in your VPC, or on-prem — move when you’re ready."
- "Fallbacks keep your app online when other vendors silently drop requests."

Role-play scripts (30–60s snippets):
- SDR (hunting email): "Most teams we talk to underestimate inference tail risk. We help teams move from token surprises to predictable budgets with an API-first experience. Quick 20-minute sync to show your last-week token heatmap?"
- AE (objection-handling): "If cost is the concern, let's run a 2-week capacity pilot and instrument actual traffic — we'll show the true unit economics and a tailored Optimize plan."
- SE (technical deep-dive): "Here’s a short demo of our fallback policy and KV cache behavior under chat workloads; if you share a representative prompt set we'll run a regression to show output parity."

Risk list & tricky competitor tactics (how to detect and respond):
- Competitor uses "creative" per-token math (e.g., counts tokens differently): "Ask for a sample request profile and raw logs — we’ll normalize and show the real delta."
- Incumbent promises unlimited throughput but hides throttles in docs: "Request real SLA incidents and ask for a recent incident postmortem."
- Vendor pushes on-hosted-only vs private as a cost argument: "Highlight the migration friction and long-term op savings of consistent API + private option."

Field playbook: immediate next actions for deals where these signals appear
1) Book a 20m discovery with SE + AE; collect representative prompt set and traffic shape.
2) Proposal: offer a 14-day pilot with instrumentation (cost + latency + quality) and a one-page migration plan.
3) Sequencing: sales -> quick pilot -> dedicated contract option -> private onboarding if required.

Attachments & assets to use in calls:
- One-pager: "Predictable Inference Economics" (internal)
- Demo scripts: fallback-demo.md, optimize-sim.xlsx
- Customer proof: anonymized case study (healthcare-client-p99-latency.pdf)

Open questions / items for marketing to produce:
- Short competitive cheat-sheet (visual) comparing: per-token pricing, SLA types, private option, observability, Optimize tooling.
- 2-slide battle slide for field decks: "Why predictable economics beats cheapest token" + pilot offer.

Action items (owner):
- SE team: gather 3 reproducible demo recordings for fallback and p99 consistency (owner: Diego).
- Marketing: generate 1-slide competitive visual and a 1-page pilot template (owner: Priya).
- Sales Ops: create a pilot SKUs pack with pricing bands and legal checklist (owner: Samir).

Notes (tone & content guidance):
- This doc is intentionally tactical and lightweight — use fragments in Slack for rapid sharing.
- Keep claims backed by a pilot or internal telemetry; avoid absolute numbers in public slides without sign-off.
